key_insight: Pearson type IV heavy-tailed, asymmetric fluctuations can arise from state-dependent diffusion even with a symmetric linear restoring drift.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a stochastic basis for modeling asymmetric, extreme fluctuations in non-equilibrium flows and space plasma turbulence.
method: Derive Pearson type IV stationary distributions from linear-drift, quadratic-diffusion Fokker–Planck dynamics.
Establish necessary and sufficient emergence conditions beyond the linear–quadratic construction.
Obtain closed-form distribution statistics and a moment recurrence relation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical derivations, linking heavy tails to diffusion curvature and asymmetry to its gradient, but describes no empirical or numerical validation.
watch_item: Check which moments exist before using skewness or kurtosis, since heavy tails impose finite-order moment cutoffs.
paper_title: A Drift-Diffusion Approach for Pearson Type IV Heavy-Tail Distributions
